name: x402node Website URL Status Check
description: Probe any public URL for its live HTTP status. Returns status code, OK flag, redirect info, final URL, content-type, server header, and response time (ms). A true website uptime / health / dead-link / redirect-chain monitor for arbitrary targets.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/url/check-status?url=<TARGET_URL> (x402-paid, no body). Target passed as ?url= query param; include the scheme (https://).
usage.outputShape: url, status, statusText, ok, redirected, finalUrl, contentType, contentLength, server, responseTimeMs, meta.source, timestamp
quirks: MUST pass the target as a ?url= query param. The registry surface shows a bare GET with a 'discoverable' http schema and no documented params; calling with no url param checks nothing useful.
Pass the full URL including scheme (https://). Response echoes finalUrl with a trailing slash added (https://example.com -> https://example.com/).
x402 v1 ONLY: agentcash MCP fetch rejects this endpoint ('not supported by agentcash, only x402 v2'). Pay via qa-pay / an x402 v1-capable client instead.
contentLength may be null even on a 200 (e.g. Cloudflare-fronted hosts).
Observed cost ~$0.0038 USDC on Base (price advertised as 'Varies').

Output: url, status, statusText, ok, redirected, finalUrl, contentType, contentLength, server, responseTimeMs, meta.source, timestamp

name: AgentOracle Service Health Heartbeat
description: Live self-health snapshot of the AgentOracle service itself: operational/degraded/down status, tracked-token count, last ingestion timestamp, ingestion error counter, process uptime (seconds), and API version. A cheap heartbeat to call before issuing larger AgentOracle queries — NOT a checker for arbitrary external URLs.

usage.callShape: GET https://aiagentoracle.ai/api/v1/status (x402-paid, no body, no params).
usage.outputShape: status (operational|degraded|down), tokenCount, lastIngestion (date-time|null), ingestionErrors, uptime (seconds), version
quirks: Takes NO input — it reports the PROVIDER's own service health, not an arbitrary target URL. Do not pass ?url=; it is ignored.
This was mis-bundled with the x402node URL checker; it is a different operation entirely (provider heartbeat, not website monitor).
x402 v2 (network eip155:8453). Pays cleanly via agentcash MCP fetch.
ingestionErrors can be a large nonzero number on a still-'operational' status (observed 5538 errors while operational) — status reflects liveness, not data freshness.

name: x402 Service Monitor
description: Monitor x402 endpoints — quality/latency, webhooks, and forensics.

url.description: The x402 endpoint URL to watch.

webhookUrl.description: Where x402station will POST alert payloads. Must be reachable from the public internet.

signals.description: Optional. Defaults to ['dead', 'zombie', 'decoy_price_extreme']. Whitelisted to known signal vocabulary so a typo doesn't silently never fire.

secret.description: 64-char hex HMAC seed. Returned ONCE here. Store it.

endpointKnown.description: true if the watched URL is in our catalog. false ⇒ alerts will fire only after ingest picks the URL up.

deliveryFormat.description: Documents how to verify HMAC signatures + the JSON shape of alert payloads.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402station.io/api/v1/watch with JSON body {url, webhookUrl, signals?}
usage.outputShape: body.watchId (uuid), body.secret (one-time 64-char hex HMAC seed), body.expiresAt, body.signals[], body.alertsPaid, body.alertsRemaining, body.endpointKnown, body.deliveryFormat (HMAC verification + alert payload shape), body.statusUrl, body.unsubscribeUrl
quirks: webhookUrl is REQUIRED and must be a publicly reachable URL — x402station POSTs HMAC-SHA256-signed alert payloads there when signals fire. The registration call itself is synchronous and returns immediately even if the webhook is not yet live.

body.secret is a 64-char hex HMAC seed returned ONLY ONCE in this response — store it; you need it to verify alert signatures (sha256=<hmac-hex> over raw body, constant-time compare) and to access statusUrl/unsubscribeUrl (?secret=...).

Optional signals[] defaults to ['dead','zombie','decoy_price_extreme']; must be drawn from the fixed enum (e.g. dead, zombie, slow, suspicious_high_price, proxy_markup, wildcard_402, spa_fallback, etc.) — typos are rejected, not silently ignored.
endpointKnown:false means the watched URL is not yet in x402station's catalog, so alerts only fire after their ingest picks it up.
Response includes idempotentReplay flag and alertsPaid/alertsRemaining (100 alerts included per watch). Watch has an expiresAt (~30 days out).
A request-bin / webhook.site style webhookUrl can be flagged by safety classifiers as exfil-shaped; use a legitimate public endpoint you control.
usage.guide: POST to https://x402station.io/api/v1/watch with a JSON body containing the x402 endpoint URL to monitor (url) and a publicly reachable webhookUrl where alerts will be delivered; optionally pass signals[] from the documented enum (defaults to dead/zombie/decoy_price_extreme). The call costs $0.01 USDC on Base and returns synchronously with a watchId and a one-time HMAC secret — store the secret immediately, as it is required to verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature on incoming alert webhooks and to call the statusUrl/unsubscribeUrl. When a watched signal fires, x402station POSTs a signed payload to your webhookUrl (up to 5 retries, ~5min apart). 100 alerts are included per watch and it expires in ~30 days.
